page_title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today

summary.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
summary.one_liner: A KrebsOnSecurity investigative report on the alleged ShinyHunters extortion leader "Rey," his detention in Jordan, and the group's exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability (CVE-2026-35273).
takeaways: ShinyHunters allegedly exploited the Oracle PeopleSoft flaw CVE-2026-35273 as a zero-day from June, mass-compromising systems across many sectors.
Mandiant released web application firewall rules as interim mitigation; attackers reportedly bypassed them with a URL-encoding trick.
A suspected ShinyHunters member, identified as Rey (Saif Al-din Khader), was reportedly detained in Amman and is cooperating with the FBI.
Boeing confirmed extortion attempts involving data from its former subsidiary Jeppesen ForeFlight, which reported no operational impact.
After a Dutch arrest in September, the group's brand was taken over by Rey, who taunted the FBI and Cl0p on social media.
summary.summary: This Krebs on Security news article reports on the alleged leader of the ShinyHunters data-theft and extortion group, a teenager identified as "Rey," who was reportedly detained in Jordan while cooperating with the FBI. It traces the group's activity, including exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability (CVE-2026-35273) that Mandiant and GTIG documented as mass-exploited across many sectors, and an attempted extortion of a Boeing unit, Jeppesen ForeFlight. The piece draws on prior reporting, public social media posts, and a GitHub blog, plus sources and company statements. The page text is the article body and does not cover the PHP flaw named in the page title.
